# PR #179 correctness verdict

**BLOCK** at `81dd2f36fc76f441774b7a01f5bc72473be3a424`.

The two modified readiness polls preserve their assertions and use meaningful positive needles. One remaining send-then-fixed-sleep capture has the same F123 race and contradicts the requested remaining-waits check.

## F001, P2: the watchdog recovery test still snapshots before echo is known ready

watchdog_expiry_before_disable_cannot_strand_input ends with send-keys for `HUMAN-KEYBOARD-WORKS`, a fixed 50 ms sleep, one capture-pane, then a contains assertion (`crates/tmux/tests/adapter.rs:875-881`).

As with the repaired boundary-text test, tmux accepting the keys does not guarantee that the pane has echoed them within 50 ms. Delayed scheduling can therefore fail a correct watchdog recovery at its final human-keyboard assertion. This is the same positive-render-readiness pattern, not a deliberate observation that nothing happened.

Use the new condition-based capture helper for that final assertion, retaining the unique keyboard marker and existing watchdog/input-state checks. The delayed-send witness should cover this assertion too, not only the changed capture test.

This is a source-derived counterexample; no local delay injection, live tmux or Cargo run was performed. The reported delayed wrapper demonstrates the general race but was applied by the author to the boundary capture body, not this remaining tail.

## Confirmed non-vacuous checks

- capture_until_contains calls capture with u32::MAX on every iteration, refuses read failures, and returns only after the literal nonempty `boundary-text` is present. It cannot substitute an empty capture on timeout; the panic includes the needle and last capture.
- The test still explicitly asserts a zero-line request returns the empty string and a one-line request equals the last available line of the positive oversized capture. Moving the contains condition into the polling helper does not delete the oversized positive witness or weaken those assertions.
- The fixture's pane runs cat and this test types the marker without Enter. The marker is the intended terminal echo, not a printed command containing a misleading completion token.
- Server::start captures its first isolated pane until `%end 1 2 3` is present. Its startup printf emits that literal output; the command is supplied as the pane's launch command, not echoed as typed input. The forked capture is not a control-protocol reply containing an incidental frame marker.
- Both added loops use 20 ms retry sleeps and 15 s budgets. Deadlines are checked between completed reads; they do not independently cancel a blocked child read.

## Other waits and scope

Remaining sleeps are not all removable: the no-byte/no-extra-Enter assertions, hostile-name no-job check, controlled SIGSTOP duration, deliberate race spacing, and foreign-window-survival observation windows have timing or negative-observation purposes.

**N001, separate cleanup-readiness limit:** control_mode.rs:695 still waits 300 ms after dropping an adapter before asserting that _pij has disappeared. That is an expected asynchronous cleanup transition, not a render wait, and can also be made condition-based. It is distinct from F001's exact F123 send/echo race; this verdict does not demand deleting every intentional sleep.

The D-WB-62 edit keeps F64 unowned and distinguishes server-exited failures from render readiness; it does not claim this PR resolves those failures.

## Proof and cost

Exact-head CI [42447292932](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42447292932) passed. JUnit artifact 13604785075 contains **2201 cases, zero failures/errors**, including all **39 adapter** and **17 control_mode** cases. Passing the remaining fixed-delay test on one runner does not establish readiness under delayed echo.

The author reports an injected 0.5 s delayed send: the old boundary test failed, the new one passed; an impossible needle also failed with the last capture. The control-mode impossible-needle mutation failed its parity test. Those scratch witnesses were not committed or rerun by this reviewer.

No production code, daemon loop or launch site changes. Each test-only poll can attempt roughly 50 reads/second, less actual child latency. The normal adapter poll uses its warmed control client, with fork fallback if unavailable; Server::start deliberately launches one raw capture child per attempt. Startup reads bypass the logging wrapper and occur before the measured adapter-operation window, so the existing launch-count assertions retain their meaning. No live fleet measurements were run here.

The checkout is clean/detached, matches the remote authorized full head and GitHub reports CLEAN. No local product tests, builds, dependencies, worktree mutation or shared-server action was performed.
